steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Oh, Chief of the MBCC, it's a pleasure to meet you. It's been no easy feat to secure an audience with you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Given the special status of Sinners, our visit approval process must be stringent. This is for the protection of both parties involved. I trust you understand.
In the meeting room, the merchant brazenly scrutinizes both you and Dove, behaving so arrogantly that he's barely trying to hide the powerful connections backing him.

Whatever this merchant and his backers might be plotting, he does have legitimate trading credentials in WhiteSands, and the background check confirms his extensive knowledge of Outlands' current situation and trade networks.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: And this must be... Miss Dove?

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Hello, sir. I'm Dove. It's a pleasure to meet you.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Young, pretty, and obedient. Perfect. In our line of work, trustworthiness is key, and a young lady like yourself... Tsk tsk, you'll be quite a valuable asset.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Your Chief must have already briefed you about why I'm here, yes?
Under his appraising gaze sizing her up like merchandise, Dove shows not the slightest hint of displeasure, the perfect curve of her smile never faltering.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Yes, Chief has already told me. Actually, this is my first time meeting someone like yourself, a big-time trader who works across WhiteSands and Outlands.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Before meeting you, I was worried I might be unqualified. Someone like me who knows nothing other than delivering mail... could I really be of any help to you?

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Haha, you sure are humble! Miss Dove, you're quite different from your Chief here. You're very pleasant and down-to-earth.
Dove's practiced flattery has the merchant beaming with satisfaction. He nods approvingly, his tone growing even more pompous.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: No need to sell yourself short. You might think delivering mail is just a trivial job, but that's because you don't know the inner workings. In today's market, there's quite a profit to be made there.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Really? I'm afraid I don't quite understand... I know so little about business matters...

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Ah, you'll understand once I explain! I'm confident this business of mine will interest you, as long as you don't have... other reservations!
The merchant shoots you a meaningful glance. Rather than a mere suggestion, it's an unmistakable warning forbidding your intervention.
You smile back at him, pretending not to have noticed his boastful attitude.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: My duties require me to be present throughout your meeting, but within reasonable bounds, I will respect Dove's personal choices.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Well, it'd be fantastic if you could keep your word, Chief.

The merchant doesn't hide his distrust of you and the Bureau, attempting to drive a wedge between you and Dove. But this plays right into your hands. You'd be even more pleased if he could be more blatant.
After all, you've brought Dove here just so the merchant can provoke her with his contemptible arrogance, to stir whatever spark of the messenger dream that might still remain in her heart.
You don't think that Dove has chosen to stay in this profession after all her disillusionment purely out of malice and vengeance. The merchant is simply your pawn in this psychological gambit.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Chief ${PlayerName} is very kind, and we Sinners all trust him. If I have to make any decisions, I should certainly consider his opinion!
steps.female_content: Chief ${PlayerName} is very kind, and we Sinners all trust her. If I have to make any decisions, I should certainly consider her opinion!

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Consider his opinion? Hah! I'm afraid your Chief knows nothing about business!
steps.female_content: Consider her opinion? Hah! I'm afraid your Chief knows nothing about business!

steps.content: Whether or not Dove perceives the hidden agendas between you and the merchant, she maintains her gentle yet firm demeanor as she steps in to smooth over the tension.
Oblivious to your true relationship with Dove, the merchant grows agitated at her convincing display of loyalty. He waves his hand dismissively, eager to regain control of the conversation.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Let me tell you something: you don't realize how much sway DisCity holds in Outlands and WhiteSands unless you're a businessman!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Hmm... I've read in books that DisCity has brought hope for humanity's survival. That's why many people in Outlands look up to its prosperity.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Oh, they don't just look up to it! Those country bumpkins from Outlands would risk their lives just to sneak into DisCity!
Frustrated by Dove's naivety, the man decides to spell things out.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: But those backwaters are dirt poor and isolated. Some of these so-called cities can't even match up to a satellite town of DisCity! Things like personal devices, internet... Tsk, they've got none of those!

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: They still rely on people running around on foot to deliver messages. These so-called mail carriers... belong in a history textbook if you ask me! If they want to know what's happening in the outside world, they can only rely on merchant caravans like ours!

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Sometimes we do help deliver mail on the side. But who'd want to waste time tracking people down and delivering these trivial messages? Hah! It's not worth the costs even for those expensive handicrafts! That being said...
He pauses deliberately, giving Dove a chance to fill in. Playing along, she claps her hands with an expression of sudden realization and chimes in excitedly.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: If I could use my ability to forge reply letters... we could easily trick them into supplying us with these handicrafts and make a fortune!

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Hmm, you're quite sharp. It's always a joy to talk to someone with business acumen. So you get it now, right? If you work for me, all you'll need to do is write a few letters. No need to wear yourself out delivering mail.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: I've seen plenty of fools risk their lives on their mail routes through WhiteSands. Some of them never made it back alive. I'm known for taking good care of my staff, and I won't let you do anything that stupid.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: After all, one doesn't meet someone with your insight and vision every day, sir.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: All it takes is forging a few letters. It's a great way to save costs and avert risks. If someone else had thought of such a brilliant method, they would've made a fortune off the Outlanders by now.
Her flattery really strokes the merchant's ego. He clears his throat before correcting Dove in a pretentiously serious voice.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: That's not all! Don't forget about all those village chiefs in Outlands! These leaders also have to spend money on our good news just to keep their ignorant masses happy!

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Letters may be old-fashioned, but they have their uses! They're tangible proof, and word spreads quickly through a village! Sign one off with someone's relative's name and you've got the whole village fooled!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: I see, you are really well-versed in this subject. I totally overlooked that. Since letters are so valuable, shouldn't we charge down payments from those Outlanders?

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: And after they pay us, we'll promise to deliver letters regularly! That way we can easily cut and run whenever we want! I mean, even if we don't... who knows how long these Outland villages will even last?

The two discuss their schemes enthusiastically as if you weren't there. You observe silently as their conversation sinks deeper into moral depravity, crossing one line after another, yet Dove seems perfectly at ease with it.
What you see makes you question your judgment. Were you wrong from the start? Is there even any point in trying to test Dove's true nature?

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Exactly! It's almost like these Outlanders are delusional! They're just a bunch of lowlifes who might not even live long, yet they dare to dream about living in DisCity, chasing their ridiculous DisCity dream!

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Haha, do they really think they deserve it? The DisCity dream belongs to us, the people of DisCity. Only businessmen like us who profit off Outlands deserve to be real idealists!

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Those Outlanders should be grateful we let them be DisCity's cash machine!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: ...You're absolutely right, sir.

Dove keeps smiling and agreeing with the merchant's increasingly outrageous statements, though her enthusiasm has notably dimmed. The merchant remains pleased, making a show of modesty with a wave of his hand while barely containing his smugness.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Miss Dove, you're smart enough to know how to play the game. I can tell we're going to have a wonderful partnership!

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Tell you what, I've been wanting to get into this business for a while now. I've tried working with some local messengers before... but they were all too rigid and frankly just dumb! No wonder Outlanders are dirt poor!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: ...Did they all decline your offer?
You might be imagining it, but Dove's voice is sounding a bit tremulous. Yet when you pick up on this subtle change and turn to look at her face, you find only her usual radiant smile.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: You bet they did! Every single one of them spouted nonsense about their duty and code of conduct and all that... like writing a few fake letters would kill them. A messenger's professionalism? Can you eat that? Does it pay?

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: I met this idiot in WhiteSands once. Now that was memorable. Half of this messenger's body was already buried in the sand, yet he was still grabbing at me. What did he say again...

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Oh! He was telling me not to worry about him, he was dying anyway, and just take the letters and deliver them... What else? Oh right, he said the whole village was waiting for this letter that could save lives.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: ...So, did you end up delivering that poor soul's letter, sir?

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Like I would! I just walked away. He kept calling out and begging until I couldn't hear him anymore! Hah, it was so stupid it made me laugh. Their whole village wasn't worth half of the deal I just made.

Perhaps emboldened by your silence or pleased by Dove's apparent approval, the merchant grows increasingly unrestrained, his gaping mouth spewing nothing but selfishness and greed he takes such pride in.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: A month later when I passed by again, there wasn't a single living person left in that town! You know, I kinda regret just walking away like that. I should've looted whatever valuables were left!
The merchant's cruel laughter bounces around the meeting room like a dropped ball that no one moves to catch, echoing until it finally sinks into dead silence.

The person who has been playing along and catching the ball this whole time suddenly falls silent, head bowed. You instinctively turn to Dove, and this time you see her clenched fists trembling uncontrollably.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: How dare you... How dare you?!

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Wahhhh!

Raw, unbridled rage surges through the other end of the shackles, so intense it makes your breath catch. The Sinner's rage, suppressed throughout the entire conversation, has finally reached its breaking point. She's about to lose control!

Countless letters shoot out of her messenger bag, sweeping through the meeting room like a hurricane. The swirling letters overturn the desk and chairs, then, at their master's command, all aim at the man cowering on the floor!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: How dare you look down on that messenger?! How dare you call him stupid?! Do you really think everyone is as greedy, shameless, vicious, and cold-blooded as you?!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: People... scum like you shouldn't be allowed to exist in this world!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Dove, stop! You can't lose control again!
But Dove, consumed by rage, pays no heed to your intervention, only inching closer toward the merchant.
If she actually harms him, as a Sinner, who is already in a precarious position, she will suffer irreversible consequences. You must stop Dove before she completely loses control.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Let go of me! Let, nngh...!
Crimson thorns pierce through her fragile frame, but Dove, usually submissive to the shackles, now erupts with a burst of powerful resistance.
To prevent Dove from breaking free, you're forced to unleash the shackles once more. This time, with your firm determination, you finally seal away her special power with the shackles.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: You money-grubbing scum! You're nothing but a parasite feeding off people's hard-earned savings!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: How dare you look down on that messenger who sacrificed his life for his duty! How dare you open your filthy mouth to judge all the messengers who deliver hope to everyone!

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Ahhh, stay back! Don't come near me!!! Guards! Where are the guards?!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Drop the act! You're nothing but a cowardly, greedy cockroach obsessed with forgery. You make me sick just looking at you!

Without her special power, Dove is just a frail girl who cannot break free from your restraint. All she can do is let out a barrage of furious screams that tears through the air and through her mask of gentle grace.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Messengers... are people who deliver emotions and connect souls. Any one of them is a hundred times more noble than you!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Calling yourself an idealist... Don't you dare sully that word!
Surging rage twists Dove's delicate features as her words, sharp as needles, seem to pierce not only the merchant but herself as well.
After that, she falls silent, though her chest still heaves heavily. Through the shackles, you sense the undisguised turmoil of emotions, and your suspicions are finally confirmed.
For all her apparent indifference, a small flame of her dream still burns within Dove's heart, even if she refuses to acknowledge or face it.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Huff... huff... Well, well! So this is how the Bureau manages its Sinners?! What were you thinking, letting this unstable monster meet with me?!
The merchant finally snaps out of his shock, jumping up and venting his terror and rage. Still trembling with fear, he only dares to accuse you both while standing behind the couch.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I deeply regret this incident. As Chief, I take full responsibility, and according to the Bureau's regulations, Sinner Dove will be placed under confinement.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Confinement? She just attempted murder and you're only locking her in a cell?! First you failed to protect your business partner's life, and now you're covering for the culprit?!
You cut him off firmly.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Allow me to correct you, sir. You've misunderstood something. Dove will be disciplined for acting without permission. It has nothing to do with whether or not you were her target.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Furthermore, I never promised you any business cooperation. The Bureau has no interest in dealing with a businessman who discriminates against Outlanders and runs illegal operations like yourself. Nightingale, please escort the gentleman out.
Ignoring the merchant's reaction, you use your communicator to summon Nightingale waiting outside.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Hey, don't forget who sent me here! Don't get too big-headed just because you're Chief. You should know your place...

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Sir, visit time is over. Please come with me. I'll show you the way out of the Bureau.
You've heard such threats countless times before, and your capable adjutant will handle them appropriately. Leaving the merchant's empty threats behind, you lead Dove out of the meeting room.
On the way to the confinement cell, she follows you in unusual silence, head bowed and completely docile.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I thought you said idealism was dead and pointless. Deceiving others with forged letters to feed your vanity and sense of superiority, isn't this the way of life you've chosen?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If that's the case... why did you get so worked up? Where did this rage come from? You know that for a Sinner, negative emotions are both a source of power and a poison that corrupts the body and soul, don't you?
You speak at a measured pace, but the questions you've thrown at Dove are like stones dropped into a bottomless pit. You don't hear a single echo, even as you reach the confinement cell.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: It's okay if you don't have the answers now.

choices.text: It's okay if you don't have the answers now.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: After all, I guess you're not sure either. Perhaps some alone time will give you a chance to think these questions through.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: ...Wait!
Having kept her silence all this time, Dove finally calls out to stop you. You turn around and wait for her question, but what she says at last seems both relevant and irrelevant at the same time.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: I offended the guest and caused such a mess... Is this really it? Just confinement?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: According to the regulations, this is sufficient punishment for a single instance of rash behavior. Sticking to the rules is my duty as Chief.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Regulations? Duty? You talk about these things, but do you think that bastard will care about any of that? Aren't you afraid he'll...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I will act according to my principles. As for whether others follow them or not, that's beyond my control and won't affect my decisions.
She falls silent and walks into the confinement cell of her own accord. You close the door and turn to leave, but you can feel her lingering gaze following you.
